result: People with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) have significantly more PcrV-specific circulating B cells compared to non-CF controls. After enrichment, PcrV-specific cells made up ≥5% of B cells in 71% of CF donors and demonstrated significant expansion in cell number over non-CF individuals, with similar differences when normalized to lymphocyte count.
evaluation: Both reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. Reviewer 1 states 'The data are solid' and Reviewer 2 notes 'the authors' conclusion is supported by solid data analysis.' Neither reviewer questions the expansion of PcrV-specific B cells in CF donors compared to controls shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

result: The authors developed and validated a fluorophore-linked tetramer reagent to detect and isolate PcrV-specific B cells, using single-cell sorting and paired-chain sequencing to identify BCR variable region sequences. The tetramer specificity was demonstrated by mouse immunization experiments showing expanded populations of class-switched PcrV+ B cells.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly praises the 'high efficiency of isolating antigen-specific BCRs using an antigenic hook' as a strength. Neither reviewer questions the tetramer methodology or its validation. The approach is accepted as technically sound.

result: The authors derived multiple high-affinity anti-PcrV monoclonal antibodies from PcrV-specific B cells across three CF donors. From 20 expressed BCRs, 60% showed at least moderate PcrV binding and 35% showed high-affinity binding. Several mAbs (408, 411) exhibited binding comparable to the engineered control V2L2MD/gremubamab.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'the authors' conclusion is supported by data' and notes the high efficiency of the approach. Neither reviewer challenges the binding data or antibody generation results. The methodology and binding characterization are accepted without critique.

result: Five CF-derived mAbs (408, 411, 437, 439, 442) were tested in a murine pneumonia challenge model. All five produced significant reductions in lung bacterial burden at 24 hours, with ~2 log reduction compared to controls. The CF-derived mAbs performed equivalently to the positive control V2L2MD mAb.
evaluation: While Reviewer 2 acknowledges 'Four of five recombinantly expressed PcrV-specific mAbs exhibited anti-PA activity in a murine pneumonia challenge model as potent as the V2L2MD mAb,' they raise a critical concern: 'therapeutic potency for these isolated mAbs is uncertain as the gremubamab has failed in Phase 2 trials.' The reviewer questions whether the mAbs have 'therapeutic potential better than the gremubamab' and notes they are 'as potent as, but not superior to' the failed clinical candidate.

result: BCR sequencing revealed predominantly germline sequences with little somatic hypermutation in Donor 1, while MBCs from Donors 2 and 3 showed average somatic hypermutation loads of 2.5% and <1% respectively. There was significant breadth in V gene usage within and between donors.
evaluation: Neither reviewer questions these sequencing findings. Reviewer 2 states 'the authors' conclusion is supported by solid data analysis,' which encompasses the BCR repertoire characterization. The data on somatic hypermutation and V gene diversity are accepted without challenge.

result: The antibody discovery strategy was extremely efficient compared to standard methods, requiring expression of very few (<12) BCRs from each donor to yield protective anti-pseudomonal mAbs, versus screening hundreds to thousands of hybridomas in traditional approaches.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly identifies 'High efficiency of isolating antigen-specific BCRs using an antigenic hook' as a strength. The efficiency claim is supported by the data showing 5 of 5 tested mAbs were protective, which reviewers do not dispute.

result: The anti-PcrV mAbs isolated using this approach matched the in vivo performance of V2L2MD IgG (the binding component of gremubamab). However, V2L2MD was effective in animal models but the bi-specific antibody gremubamab failed Phase 2 clinical trials. Whether human MBC-derived mAbs will be more effective clinically remains uncertain, though they have theoretical advantages including reduced immunogenicity.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 directly addresses this issue as a weakness: 'it is unclear whether PcrV-specific mAbs isolated in this study have therapeutic potential better than the gremubamab, which has failed in Phase 2 trials.' The reviewer requests 'Clarification of this concern by revising the text or providing experimental results that show better potential than gremubamab.' This indicates the therapeutic potential claim is uncertain and requires additional support.

result: In Donor 1, only two PcrV-specific B cells expressed canonical MBC surface markers (CD21+CD27+), and the surface-expressed isotype of all PcrV-specific B cells was IgM, indicating most were not classical memory B cells.
evaluation: Neither reviewer questions these phenotypic findings. The observation that protective antibodies came from non-classical MBCs is accepted as part of the 'solid data' noted by Reviewer 2.

result: The study provides new insight into the cellular sources of the humoral response to PA in pwCF, demonstrating that B cells with the capacity to produce functional anti-PA antibodies are present in peripheral blood, expanding on prior studies limited to measuring secreted antibodies.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 states 'the protective antibodies identified in this study could be useful for protection against PA,' implicitly accepting the biological insights. Neither reviewer challenges the characterization of the B cell response in CF patients.

result: The results reveal a diverse PcrV-specific repertoire in pwCF and, combined with prior work on other pathogens, suggest human antigen-specific B cells are an underutilized high-yield resource for discovering new treatments for infectious diseases.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 affirms 'the authors' conclusion is supported by data' and identifies the efficiency of the approach as a strength. The broader conclusion about B cells as a resource for antibody discovery is implicitly supported by the reviewers' acceptance of the methodology and results.
